Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows a prominent opacity at the right lung apex with associated destruction/erosion of the adjacent first and second ribs, which is the classic radiographic appearance of a Pancoast tumour (superior sulcus tumour). This diagnosis aligns with the patient's history of long-term smoking and neurological symptoms (disorientation), whereas the other options do not typically present with this specific combination of apical mass and rib destruction.
